CELL_C_trendline_proximity_admissibility.question: Among decision rows the population backtest already evaluated (CELL_A's run), does trendline_detector-measured proximity to ANY detected line (nearest_distance_pct from trendline_state_for_decision_row) correlate with trade outcome?
CELL_C_trendline_proximity_admissibility.method: For every CELL_A trade, compute trendline state (backtest/lib/trendline_detector, wick mode, default grammar, ~3-trading-day lookback) AS OF the entry bar via annotate_decisions_with_trendline_state (strictly post-hoc, reads bars <= entry bar only -- C6). Bucket by abs(nearest_distance_pct) into near/mid/far terciles. Report per-bucket n / total / WR / per-trade, plus Spearman(bucket-rank, pnl) with a shuffle-null 90% interval (same method as trend-alignment-correlation.md, reused for consistency across correlational studies in this codebase).
CELL_C_trendline_proximity_admissibility.kill_criteria_ladder: SAME shape as trend-alignment-correlation.md's P1 ladder: (1) OOS-half positive AND beats shuffle-null, (2) monotonic-ish (<=1 adjacent-bucket inversion), (3) survives drop-top-3-per-bucket, (4) both chronological halves same sign. ALL FOUR required for SUPPORTED; any failure = KILL (informational, not re-run).
CELL_C_trendline_proximity_admissibility.not_a_flip: Even a SUPPORTED verdict here does not itself change any live filter -- it would only qualify a SEPARATELY pre-registered Phase 2 proposal for HOW an admissibility filter would be wired (mirrors trend-alignment-correlation.md's own OP-16 eval-first framing exactly).
